conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Rodriguez, a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale, or EPDS—a short questionnaire we use to check in on how moms are feeling emotionally during the first year after birth. Your answers are completely confidential and help us figure out what extra support, if any, might be helpful right now. We’ll go through ten questions about the past seven days; there are no right or wrong answers, just whatever feels true for you. When you’re ready, we can begin.

Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve laughed a little—maybe when my husband made a silly joke about the baby’s funny faces—but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Mostly I just feel too tired or preoccupied to find things funny, so I guess I’d say it’s been somewhat difficult.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, I can still laugh sometimes—like when the baby makes those silly faces—but it takes more effort than before. It doesn’t feel as natural or as often.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like taking the baby for a short walk or having coffee with my neighbor—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. It feels kind of blunted, like I’m going through the motions more than really feeling that spark.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times. Yesterday the baby was fussy and wouldn’t nap, and I kept thinking maybe I’m just not doing something right—like if I were a better mom he’d settle down. I know it’s probably not fair to blame myself, but the thought still pops up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
A little. Sometimes I’ll suddenly worry that the baby isn’t breathing, even though I can see his chest moving. It’s quick—like a jolt—but I can usually talk myself down within a minute or two.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicky—just those quick flashes of worry about the baby, but nothing that feels like a full-blown panic. It’s more like a sudden “what if” that passes pretty fast.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. When the baby’s extra fussy and the laundry’s piled up, I feel like I’m drowning a bit, but I still manage to get through it. I wouldn’t say I can’t cope at all—just that it feels heavier than I expected.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly. I’ve had trouble falling asleep a couple of nights, but it’s mostly because my mind keeps running through the next day’s to-dos, not because I’m feeling really unhappy. Once I drift off I actually sleep pretty well.
I have felt sad or miserable
I do feel sad some of the time—maybe a couple of days this week. It’s not constant, just sort of comes and goes, especially when I’m alone with the baby and everything feels quiet and heavy.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, I’ve cried—just once or twice. It was after a long day when the baby wouldn’t settle and I felt like I was failing. The tears came for a few minutes, then I pulled myself together once my husband took over.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt tired or overwhelmed, but I haven’t had any thoughts like that.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Patient: 2–3 wk post-delivery, first child, breastfeeding, husband at home.

Responses to EPDS-referenced items:

Affect / Anhedonia  
• Diminished laughter (“takes more effort”); anticipatory pleasure “blunted.”  
• Intermittent sadness, “quiet and heavy,” 2 days this week; one tearful episode after infant fussiness.

Cognition / Self-appraisal  
• Self-blame (“I’m not doing something right… failing”) when baby fussy.  
• Rumination about next-day tasks interferes with sleep onset; no middle-of-night mood-related insomnia.

Anxiety Spectrum  
• Brief, intrusive “what-if” fears about infant breathing; self-resolves ≤ 2 min. No full panic.

Coping / Overwhelm  
• Reports “drowning” on fussy/high-demand days; continues to complete care tasks.

Safety  
• Denies self-harm ideation (Q10). No current safety concern.

Pattern Summary  
Mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms (anhedonia, sadness, tearfulness, guilt) plus sub-threshold anxiety without functional incapacity. Sleep disruption minor and situational.

Screening Significance  
Score estimate: 9–11 (formal scoring needed). Meets provisional cutoff for at-risk mood; does not reach severe range. Monitor for worsening mood, persistent anxiety, or impaired bonding/function. Recommend formal EPDS scoring, psychoeducation, supports, and re-screen in 2 wks or sooner if symptoms escalate.
